standard_prerequisites.name: Strict transform as the blowup of the effective Cartier divisor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, the lemma identifying the strict transform of a divisor under a blowup, and the lemma that blowing up an effective Cartier divisor does not change the scheme
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification of the strict transform of the regular curve with the blowup of that curve in the point, hence the isomorphism statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Description of the blowup algebra and the ideal of the exceptional divisor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard description of the affine blowup algebra generated by the quotients of the maximal ideal by a chosen element, with the image of that element cutting out the exceptional divisor
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the algebra on which the comparison map is defined and the computation of the multiplicity against the exceptional fibre.

core_obligations: Choose local coordinates (proof lines 4358-4372): since the local ring of the first curve at the point is a discrete valuation ring and a quotient of the local ring of the surface, choose an element of the maximal ideal mapping to a uniformizer there, take an affine neighbourhood containing it and let the ideals of the two curves be given; after shrinking one may assume the maximal ideal is generated by the ideal of the first curve together with that element, which says that the intersection of the zero locus of the element with the first curve is the point scheme theoretically.

Identify the strict transform (proof lines 4372-4384): consequently the point is an effective Cartier divisor on the first curve, and since the strict transform of that curve is its blowup in the point, the blowup is an isomorphism onto it; the relation between the maximal ideal and the ideal of the curve together with the chosen element allows one to define a map from the blowup algebra to the quotient defining the curve by assigning to a quotient of an element of the maximal ideal the class of a suitable multiplier.

Compute the multiplicities (proof lines 4384-4390): the image of the chosen element in the blowup algebra cuts out the exceptional divisor, so the intersection multiplicity of the transform of the curve with the exceptional fibre is one; and since the ideal of a function vanishing on the second curve contains the quotients of its elements by the chosen element, choosing a function realizing the intersection multiplicity of the two curves at the point yields a function on the transform whose order there is one less, which proves the strict decrease of the multiplicity.
proof_roadmap: Choose a local equation of the first curve as a uniformizer and bring the maximal ideal into the form generated by the curve plus that element.
Use the description of the strict transform as a blowup of a Cartier divisor to get the isomorphism and to build the comparison map.
Read off the two multiplicity statements from the equation of the exceptional divisor and from the displayed quotients.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that when the strict transforms of two curves meeting at a point are formed after blowing up that point and the first curve is regular there, then the strict transform of the first curve maps isomorphically to the curve, meets the exceptional fibre in a single point with intersection multiplicity one, and against the second transform has strictly smaller intersection multiplicity than before the blowup (statement lines 4345-4356). The proof (proof lines 4358-4392) chooses a local equation of the regular curve, identifies the strict transform with a blowup of a Cartier divisor, builds an explicit map from the blowup algebra, and computes the two multiplicities. H2: a local computation with two inputs, written out in full.
